newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty International slams Spanish asylum proposal.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty International slams Spanish asylum proposal.

text.p: A Spanish proposal to deny people of one European Union nation the right to seek asylum in another contradicts human rights and could set a precedent in other areas of the world, Amnesty International warned on Friday.
The London-based international human rights organisation urged EU members to respect their international obligations and not to deny asylum rights.

"It is a core principle of international refugee law that all asylum seekers, irrespective of their country of origin, should have access to a fair and satisfactory individual asylum determination procedure," Amnesty said in a statement.

Spain requested the asylum amendment, designed to combat terrorist activities, to the Maastricht treaty at the Inter-Governmental Conference (IGC) last December. A ministerial meeting starting on February 24 will consider the proposal.
Amnesty said it understands the need for governments to prevent terrorism, but the measures adopted must conform with international human rights standards.

It added that the proposal contravenes international human rights obligations resulting from the 1951 Geneva Convention and ignores the fact that EU citizens could one day have to flee human rights violations in the current or an enlarged European Union.
Amnesty urged EU governments not to confuse the fight against terrorism with the obligation to ensure all individuals' right to seek asylum.
